description: MailBackend::blob_exists() has a default impl that always returns false (backend.rs:383). handle_email_parse calls backend.blob_exists() to distinguish 'blob not found' from 'not parsable' (email.rs:1985-1990). When a backend forgets to override blob_exists (which is easy — the trait has many methods), any parse failure for a blob that actually exists is reported as notFound instead of notParsable. The client may then re-upload the blob or report the email as missing, when in fact the blob is present but unparseable. The default should either panic with a clear message (to force backends to implement it) or the method should return Result<bool, Self::Error> so an unimplemented backend can return an error rather than a silent wrong answer. At minimum, the trait doc should say #[deprecated] or use a compile-time mechanism to make omission visible. Trigger: any backend that does not override blob_exists() + any call to Email/parse with an existing but unparseable blob.
title: blob_exists() defaults to false — Email/parse misclassifies parse errors as notFound
